title: OpenAI data shows workplace ChatGPT use is shifting from asking to doing
friendlyTitle: People at work use ChatGPT more for doing tasks than asking questions
summary: OpenAI published country-level Signals data from individual ChatGPT accounts, reporting that workplace messages are more than twice as likely to involve completing or creating something as messages outside work. It also says multimedia is the fastest-growing use case and adoption gaps between regions are narrowing.
friendlySummary: OpenAI says work messages are much more likely to ask ChatGPT to create, edit, code or analyse something. Image and other media tasks are also growing quickly.
whyItMatters: The data supports a shift from AI as an answer engine to AI as a production tool. Teams should design training and measurement around completed tasks—editing, coding and analysis—while remembering that the dataset comes from OpenAI’s own service and classifications.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A useful way to learn AI is to practise one real task from start to finish. The figures come from OpenAI, so they should be read as company research, not a complete view of all AI use.
